An interactive course for MSc students in epidemiology and public health. Twenty-five lessons, one simulated city and two running examples from environmental epidemiology. Every method is shown on data where the truth is known.

#### Example A · Heat and emergency visits {.unnumbered}
Five years of daily emergency department visits in 12 districts and 3 age groups, with temperature and PM2.5. Counts, time series, lags, nonlinear effects and maps.

:::

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}

::: {.cpanel}

#### Example B · NO₂ and childhood asthma {.unnumbered}
A birth cohort of 5,000 children with modeled and personal NO₂ exposure, socio-economic position and schools. Binary outcomes, causal inference, measurement error and disease burden.

:::

:::

:::

## How to use the course

Work through the lessons in order. Each one has interactive demonstrations narrated by a **What's happening** box; models written three ways side by side (standard notation, a model list with R, and epidemiological reporting); optional R code in closed panels; **Bayesian previews** until Part V; and a concept quiz. Underlined terms open the glossary: hover for a short definition, click for the full entry. Mark lessons as complete to track your progress here. Progress is kept in your browser only.

## Five threads through the course

[Likelihood]{style="color:var(--p1);font-weight:600"} · [Uncertainty]{style="color:var(--p2);font-weight:600"} · [Shrinkage]{style="color:var(--p3);font-weight:600"} · [Bias]{style="color:var(--p5);font-weight:600"} · [Frequentist ↔ Bayesian]{style="color:var(--p4);font-weight:600"}. Each lesson's header names the threads it develops.

## About the data

All data in this course are simulated. They resemble real environmental epidemiology data but describe no real city or person. The data files are in the course repository under `data/`, and `R/course-data.R` loads them.
